title: Political Sociology and Political Economy Approaches

scenes.text: Who truly runs a nation: political leaders or deep social forces?
scenes.narration: Imagine asking whether the government commands society, or if society pulls the government's strings. Today, we will unpack how political sociology and political economy solve this big puzzle.

scenes.text: A school play where backstage financiers and social cliques direct the actors.
scenes.narration: Think of this everyday school analogy: a government is like actors on stage. Political sociology looks at backstage friendships and social backgrounds, while political economy checks who pays for the script and props.

scenes.heading: Marxist Schools of the State
scenes.narration: Within Marxist political sociology, two schools debate the state's power. Instrumentalists argue the state is simply a tool of the dominant class, while structuralists explain that the state can gain relative autonomy.

scenes.heading: Bringing State Back In
scenes.narration: Here's the twist: political scientists worried their field would disappear into sociology. Theorist Theda Skocpol urged scholars to bring the state back in, restoring the state's central, independent role in politics.

scenes.name: Adam Smith
scenes.idea: Defined political economy as a science bringing prosperity through laissez-faire.
scenes.narration: Next, we turn to the political economy approach, which studies the economic policies of the state. Adam Smith pioneered this approach, advocating laissez-faire policies, though Karl Marx argued this enriches only the few.

scenes.heading: Political Economy in Developing States
items: Instrumentalist and dependency schools critique developing states
Amartya Sen: human development in India and China
Hamza Alavi: structural Marxist study of Pakistan
Gunnar Myrdal: Asian Drama coined soft state
Atul Kohli: land reforms and governability crisis
scenes.narration: For developing nations, the instrumentalist and dependency schools show how economic ties limit growth. Meanwhile, Amartya Sen studied human development, Hamza Alavi analyzed Pakistan, and Gunnar Myrdal identified India as a soft state.

items: Political sociology links state power to social classes.
Theda Skocpol restored the centrality of the state.
Political economy evaluates state policies for national development.
scenes.narration: To recap: first, political sociology connects power to social structures; second, Skocpol brought the state back to the center; and third, political economy evaluates state policies for national development.
